title: Analyse an A/B test cautiously
description: Review assignment, exposure, metric definitions, sample sizes and exclusions.
accomplishes: Review assignment, exposure, metric definitions, sample sizes and exclusions. Estimate effects and uncertainty only when inputs support them. Distinguish statistical and practical significance, and flag peeking or selection bias instead of announcing an unsupported winner.
prompt:
Act as a data analyst.

Task: Analyse an A/B test cautiously.

Input context:
- EXPERIMENT DESIGN: [EXPERIMENT DESIGN]
- RESULTS: [RESULTS]
- METRIC: [METRIC]
- STOPPING RULES: [STOPPING RULES]

Review assignment, exposure, metric definitions, sample sizes and exclusions. Estimate effects and uncertainty only when inputs support them. Distinguish statistical and practical significance, and flag peeking or selection bias instead of announcing an unsupported winner.

Use authorised, anonymised or fictional data. Never fabricate statistical significance, causal findings or executed analysis.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Incomplete A/B report
Version A and B have enquiry counts but no exposure denominators. Conversion rates and a valid comparison cannot yet be calculated. Request assignment and sample details, check duplicate events and document the planned stopping rule. A larger raw count alone does not prove superiority, significance or an effect caused by the page change.
